# Journal of Science Communication (JCOM)

> > An open-access, peer-reviewed journal exploring science communication research, practice, and theory across digital media, public engagement, and global contexts.

JCOM publishes research articles, practice insights, book reviews, and essays examining how science is communicated to diverse publics worldwide. The journal addresses contemporary challenges including misinformation, public trust, AI impacts, decolonization, and culturally relevant communication strategies.

## Key Topics

- Science communication theory and practice
- Public trust in science
- Misinformation and disinformation
- COVID-19 pandemic communication
- Digital and social media
- Citizen science and public engagement
- Artificial Intelligence in science communication
- Climate change communication
- Cultural context and decolonization
- Health communication
- Science journalism and media representation
- Global South perspectives
- Post-truth era challenges
- Multimodal and multilingual communication
- Public perception of science and technology

## Trust, Misinformation, and Digital Media

- [Public (dis)trust in science in digital media environments](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2309_2024_E): Special issue editorial on public trust in science amid COVID-19 & climate
- [Confronting misinformation related to health and the environment: a systematic review](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2301_2024_V01): Systematic review of strategies to combat health & environmental misinformation
- [Harnessing multimodal and multilingual science communication to combat misinformation in a diverse country setting](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2309_2024_N01): Practice insight on multilingual HIV communication in South Africa
- [How different science communicators use identity strategies to gain public trust](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2309_2024_A08): Study of identity strategies by scientists, citizens & institutions in China
- [Scientific research in news media: a case study of misrepresentation, sensationalism and harmful recommendations](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2101_2022_A06): Case study analyzing misrepresentation of scientific research in news media

## COVID-19 and Health Communication

- [COVID-19 crisis memes, rhetorical arena theory and multimodality](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_1907_2020_A01): Analysis of COVID-19 memes using rhetorical arena theory framework
- [YouTube as a source of information on chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine during the COVID-19 pandemic](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_1907_2020_A06): Quality analysis of Portuguese YouTube videos on COVID-19 treatments
- [Scratching an itch: a new perspective on health communication in Africa](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2105_2022_R02): Book review on Falade & Murire's health communication in Africa volume

## AI and Emerging Technologies

- [Science communication in the age of Artificial Intelligence](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2402_2025_E): Special issue editorial on AI's impact on science communication practices
- [Understanding public perceptions of revolutionary technology: the role of political ideology, knowledge, and news consumption](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2305_2024_A07): Study of AI perceptions in Taiwan examining ideology and knowledge factors

## Public Engagement and Citizen Science

- [Anthropomorphism and motivating participation in citizen science projects](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2308_2024_A04): Research on using anthropomorphism to boost citizen science participation
- [Measuring the impacts of participatory citizen science: lessons from the WeCount sustainable mobility project](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2305_2024_N01): Practice insight from WeCount citizen science on European sustainable mobility
- [Communicating astronomy with the public: perspectives of an international community of practice](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2003_2021_A11): Study of astronomy communicators' perspectives on public engagement

## Cultural Context and Inclusive Communication

- [Increasing culturally relevant science media coverage: exploring the outcomes of a collaboration in Puerto Rico](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2305_2024_N02): CienciaPR collaboration with El Nuevo Día for culturally relevant coverage
- [Beyond Western perspectives: inclusive insights to decolonise and transform science communication](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2301_2024_R04): Book review on decolonising science communication by Elizabeth Rasekoala

## Innovative Communication Formats and Venues

- [Can science comics aid lay audiences' comprehension of forensic science?](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2401_2025_A01): Research on The Evidence Chamber comics for jury comprehension in Scotland
- [National parks as vehicles for science communication: the science of signs](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2403_2025_A01): Content analysis of 129 interpretive signs across 11 US national parks
- [Meat as a matter of fact(s): the role of science in everyday representations of livestock production on social media](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_1806_2019_A01): Analysis of science role in social media discussions on livestock production

## Theory and Pedagogy

- [Rethinking science communication as the social conversation around science](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2003_2021_Y01): Essay on interdisciplinary trends in science communication research
- [An idea-packed guide for scientists teaching communication skills](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2301_2024_R03): Book review of Rowland & Kuchel's guide for teaching science students
